newsitem.title: UK: Texaco cuts crude runs at Rotterdam refinery - trade.
newsitem.headline: Texaco cuts crude runs at Rotterdam refinery - trade.

text.p: Texaco Inc is cutting crude oil throughput at its Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam by 20 percent in the second half of May due to poor margins, trade sources said.
Texaco has a 35 percent share of the 400,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery. British Petroleum (BP) owns the other 65 percent.
"We are going to cut crude throughput by 10 percent overall in May, that means a 20 percent cut for the second half of the month," said a trader familiar with the refinery's operations.

Refinery margins have tumbled in the past 10 days as benchmark Brent crude prices surged by about $2 a barrel, helped by tension in the Middle East and expectations of thinner North Sea supply in June.

Reuters data shows simple hydroskimming margins for a typical Rotterdam refinery turned negative earlier this week and complex cracking margins fared little better, falling from over $2 a barrel at the start of the month to around $1.30 a barrel on Thursday.
Trade sources familiar with BP's operations at Nerefco said the company had not cut crude runs.
Other refineries in the key Rotterdam region, including the giant 375,000 bpd Shell plant, were still running at full capacity on Thursday, traders said.
Total's 148,000 bpd refinery at Vlissingen was "under pressure" to cut runs but as yet had not done so, they said.
